topics.title: T1 AI and Automation 人工智能与自动化
topics.name: 人工智能与自动化

blocks.title: T1A 自动化与生产率
blocks.name: 自动化与生产率
blocks.chain: routine tasks automated → time released → attention redirected → higher productivity
blocks.model: Artificial intelligence can improve productivity by reducing the time employees spend on routine tasks. When software prepares standard reports or processes straightforward enquiries, staff have more time to investigate unusual problems and communicate with clients. A customer service team, for example, could let a system answer basic questions while experienced employees handle complicated complaints. This division of labour allows human judgement to be used where it adds greater value. The benefit is most likely to emerge when workers receive training and remain responsible for checking important decisions.
blocks.guide: 先解释节省了哪类时间，再说明时间被用于什么任务。仿写 By reducing the time spent on X, Y allows people to focus on Z.

blocks.title: T1B 岗位替代与转型失业
blocks.name: 岗位替代与转型失业
blocks.chain: tasks displaced → existing skills lose relevance → retraining takes time → unemployment risk
blocks.model: Automation may create unemployment when the tasks that disappear are different from those available in expanding industries. An employee whose experience consists mainly of entering data cannot necessarily move straight into a role involving software supervision or complex analysis. Even if the economy creates new jobs, acquiring the required skills takes time and money. Workers with limited savings may struggle to complete this transition. The employment risk therefore depends partly on how quickly technological change occurs relative to the availability of accessible retraining and suitable vacancies.
blocks.guide: 补出旧技能与新岗位之间的不匹配，避免从机器使用直接跳到永久失业。仿写 Even if X, doing Y still requires Z.

blocks.title: T1C 技术收益的分配
blocks.name: 技术收益的分配
blocks.chain: productivity gains → additional income → distribution through pay and access → inclusive benefits
blocks.model: Higher productivity does not automatically improve living standards for every employee. If a company uses new technology to increase output but directs all additional income towards owners, workers may experience heavier expectations without receiving better pay. By contrast, sharing some of the gains through training, wages or shorter working hours can make technological progress more widely beneficial. Employees who are helped to develop complementary skills are also better placed to remain valuable. The social outcome consequently depends on how firms and institutions distribute the opportunities created by automation.
blocks.guide: 区分总收益增加与谁获得收益，适用于增长和全球化。仿写 The outcome depends on how the gains from X are distributed.

topics.description: 效率提升、岗位转型与技术红利的分配。

topics.title: T2 Internet and Digital Communication 互联网与数字交流
topics.name: 互联网与数字交流

blocks.title: T2A 信息与协作成本
blocks.name: 信息与协作成本
blocks.chain: communication costs fall → knowledge and partners become accessible → wider opportunities
blocks.model: The Internet expands opportunities by lowering the cost of obtaining information and contacting other people. A learner in a small town can consult materials that would otherwise require a long journey, while a small business can communicate with customers beyond its immediate area. These connections make it easier to identify useful knowledge, compare options and coordinate activities. People can consequently participate in educational or commercial opportunities that were previously difficult to reach. Reliable access and the ability to evaluate online information remain necessary if these opportunities are to produce meaningful benefits.
blocks.guide: 用两个具体场景解释扩大机会，结尾补接入与判断能力。仿写 X enables people to access Y that would otherwise require Z.

blocks.title: T2B 数字联系与关系质量
blocks.name: 数字联系与关系质量
blocks.chain: convenient contact → relationships maintained → emotional support when interaction is meaningful
blocks.model: Digital communication can help people maintain relationships when distance prevents regular meetings. Friends who move to different cities can share everyday experiences and discuss personal difficulties through messages or video calls. Frequent contact may preserve a sense of involvement that occasional visits alone would struggle to provide. However, this benefit depends on the quality of the exchange. Brief reactions to public posts offer fewer opportunities for careful listening than a sustained private conversation. Online contact is therefore more likely to strengthen relationships when it supports meaningful interaction and mutual attention.
blocks.guide: 先承认跨距离价值，再区分联系频率与交流深度。仿写 X is more likely to strengthen Y when it supports Z.

blocks.title: T2C 比较发明的重要性
blocks.name: 比较发明的重要性
blocks.chain: broad influence → strong claim to importance → dependence on earlier inventions → qualified ranking
blocks.model: The Internet has a strong claim to being one of the most influential inventions because its applications extend across education, employment and everyday communication. A single network can support activities that once required separate institutions or physical journeys. Nevertheless, identifying the most important invention requires a clear basis for comparison. Digital services depend on electricity, without which their apparent versatility would have little practical value. The Internet may rank highly in terms of the range of activities it connects, while electricity may be more fundamental to the functioning of modern society.
blocks.guide: 回应 most 时明确比较标准，并比较真实替代项。仿写 X may rank highly in terms of A, while Y is more fundamental to B.

topics.description: 从信息获取到远程协作，辨析联系与关系。

topics.title: T3 Screen Time and Television 屏幕时间与电视
topics.name: 屏幕时间与电视

blocks.title: T3A 数字内容的学习价值
blocks.name: 数字内容的学习价值
blocks.chain: visual explanation → difficult processes become observable → understanding and curiosity
blocks.model: Carefully designed digital content can make unfamiliar ideas easier for children to understand. A short animation, for instance, can show how a natural process develops in stages, allowing learners to observe changes that a still image cannot demonstrate as clearly. Pausing the video and discussing what happens gives children opportunities to connect the explanation with what they already know. This can support understanding and stimulate further questions. Educational value therefore comes from the quality of the material and the way children engage with it, rather than simply from watching a screen.
blocks.guide: 具体解释图像如何帮助理解，并加入主动参与这一条件。仿写 X allows learners to observe Y that Z cannot demonstrate as clearly.

blocks.title: T3B 屏幕活动的替代成本
blocks.name: 屏幕活动的替代成本
blocks.chain: excessive screen use → other activities displaced → fewer developmental opportunities
blocks.model: Excessive screen use can be harmful because children have limited time for activities that support their development. If entertainment continues late into the evening, it may replace sleep, while several hours spent watching videos can reduce opportunities for exercise or conversation. The problem becomes more serious when this pattern is repeated and a balanced routine is difficult to maintain. Even suitable content can have costs when it occupies too much of the day. Judgements about screen time should therefore consider which activities are being displaced as well as what children are watching.
blocks.guide: 用时间有限解释损失，避免把内容良好直接等同于使用无限制。仿写 Even X can have costs when it displaces Y.

topics.description: 用内容质量与时间分配分析屏幕活动。

topics.title: T4 Data Privacy and Cybersecurity 数据隐私与网络安全
topics.name: 数据隐私与网络安全

blocks.title: T4A 个性化服务
blocks.name: 个性化服务
blocks.chain: relevant data → better predictions → more useful recommendations → lower search effort
blocks.model: Collecting relevant user data can improve services by helping providers understand individual needs. A learning platform that records a student's mistakes, for example, can recommend practice focused on the areas that require attention. The student then spends less time searching through unsuitable material and receives support that is more closely matched to current difficulties. Similar benefits may arise when services remember accessibility preferences or frequently used options. Such collection is easier to justify when users understand its purpose and the information retained is limited to what the service actually needs.
blocks.guide: 用学习平台说明预测如何转化成便利，结尾限定数据范围。仿写 By identifying X, a service can provide Y that is better matched to Z.

blocks.title: T4B 行为画像与操控
blocks.name: 行为画像与操控
blocks.chain: detailed profiling → vulnerabilities identified → selective messages → less independent choice
blocks.model: Extensive profiling can weaken personal autonomy when organisations use private information to exploit a person's vulnerabilities. If a platform recognises that a user responds strongly to status or appearance, it can repeatedly present messages designed to intensify those concerns. The user may feel that purchasing decisions are entirely personal while remaining unaware of how selectively the information has been arranged. This is particularly troubling when the purpose of data collection is unclear. Transparent explanations and meaningful controls can help users understand and limit this influence over their choices.
blocks.guide: 解释信息如何被选择性呈现，而不是笼统说科技控制人。仿写 People may believe X while remaining unaware of Y.

blocks.title: T4C 数据泄露与防护
blocks.name: 数据泄露与防护
blocks.chain: sensitive information concentrated → breach affects multiple activities → personal and financial harm
blocks.model: Storing large amounts of personal information in one system can increase the consequences of a security breach. Details that appear harmless separately may become useful for impersonation when combined with account records or contact information. An attacker could then use the stolen identity to gain access to other services, leaving the individual to resolve unauthorised activity and restore control. Providers therefore have responsibilities beyond making their applications convenient. Restricting access, removing information that is no longer needed and responding promptly to incidents can reduce the scale of the damage.
blocks.guide: 先解释数据组合为何放大损害，再让对策对应风险环节。仿写 Information that appears harmless separately may become useful for X when combined with Y.

topics.description: 权衡个性化便利、个人自主与数据风险。

topics.title: T5 Science and Space 科学与太空
topics.name: 科学与太空

blocks.title: T5A 基础研究与长期收益
blocks.name: 基础研究与长期收益
blocks.chain: research → new knowledge and methods → later applications → wider benefits
blocks.model: Public investment in basic research can generate benefits that are difficult to predict at the beginning of a project. Researchers investigating a scientific problem may develop a measurement technique or material that later becomes useful in another field. Because these applications can emerge after a long delay, a private company focused on immediate returns may have little reason to support the original work. Public funding can help sustain this process of discovery. Its value lies partly in creating knowledge that other researchers and organisations can use to solve future problems.
blocks.guide: 补上方法或材料向其他领域转移的过程。仿写 X may develop techniques that later become useful in Y.

blocks.title: T5B 科研投入与支出取舍
blocks.name: 科研投入与支出取舍
blocks.chain: expensive project → resources committed → other services forgone → need for comparison
blocks.model: Scientific ambition must be considered alongside other demands on public resources. A costly space programme may promise future discoveries, but the same funding could also improve services whose benefits are more immediate and predictable. Where basic healthcare or schooling remains inadequate, the opportunity cost of a speculative project may be particularly high. This does not make all space research unjustifiable. It means that governments should explain the expected public value, assess less expensive alternatives and consider whether the scale of expenditure is proportionate to the country's current needs.
blocks.guide: 比较边际投入的替代用途，不把科研与民生写成永远冲突。仿写 Where X remains inadequate, the opportunity cost of Y may be particularly high.

topics.description: 讨论科研的长期价值与公共预算的取舍。

topics.title: E1 Purpose of Education 教育的目的
topics.name: 教育的目的

blocks.title: E1A 教育的社会功能
blocks.name: 教育的社会功能
blocks.chain: knowledge and civic understanding → competent participation → productive and responsible communities
blocks.model: Education serves a social purpose by preparing people to participate competently in workplaces and communities. Employers need staff who can interpret information and solve problems, while public life depends on citizens who understand how their decisions affect others. Schools can develop these abilities through subject learning and opportunities to discuss shared responsibilities. For example, evaluating different explanations in class may help students assess public claims more carefully later in life. The contribution of education therefore extends beyond individual qualifications to the quality of economic activity and collective decision-making.
blocks.guide: 分开写职业能力与公民能力，让社会功能比提供劳动力更完整。仿写 The contribution of X extends beyond A to B.

blocks.title: E1B 教育与个人发展
blocks.name: 教育与个人发展
blocks.chain: meaningful exploration → interests identified → intrinsic motivation → sustained learning
blocks.model: Education should also give learners opportunities to discover interests that they find personally meaningful. When students can explore a subject in depth or choose a suitable project, they are more likely to take ownership of their progress. A teenager interested in local history, for instance, may willingly investigate sources beyond the minimum requirements of an assignment. This willingness to continue learning can support future adaptability. Respecting individual aspirations can therefore benefit society as well, since motivated learners may develop abilities that allow them to make valuable contributions in their chosen fields.
blocks.guide: 用自主探索解释内在动机，再连接个人与社会收益。仿写 When learners can X, they are more likely to take ownership of Y.

topics.description: 社会参与、兴趣探索与个人抱负的连接。

topics.title: E2 Curriculum 课程广度与深度
topics.name: 课程广度与深度

blocks.title: E2A 专业化学习
blocks.name: 专业化学习
blocks.chain: concentrated study → sustained practice → deeper expertise → readiness for demanding tasks
blocks.model: Specialisation can be valuable when a subject requires sustained practice before students become competent. Learners who divide their time among too many unrelated demands may struggle to move beyond basic understanding in any one area. Concentrating on a smaller set of subjects allows them to revisit difficult concepts, receive detailed feedback and attempt more demanding work. This depth can be especially useful when preparing for a profession with clear technical requirements. The appropriate degree of specialisation should nevertheless reflect the learner's stage of development and the stability of their career plans.
blocks.guide: 解释为什么时间集中能带来深度，限定年龄与职业清晰度。仿写 Concentrating on X allows learners to do Y in greater depth.

blocks.title: E2B 广泛教育与适应力
blocks.name: 广泛教育与适应力
blocks.chain: varied disciplines → different ways of reasoning → transferable judgement → adaptability
blocks.model: A broad curriculum can prepare students for situations that cannot be understood through a single subject. Studying history encourages attention to context, while science develops the habit of testing explanations against evidence. Exposure to these different approaches gives learners more than one way to examine unfamiliar problems. This matters when future jobs or social conditions change and a narrow body of knowledge becomes less sufficient. Breadth is most useful when students are helped to connect ideas across subjects, rather than being required to memorise isolated facts from an increasingly crowded timetable.
blocks.guide: 举出不同学科提供的思考方式，再说明迁移价值。仿写 Exposure to different approaches gives learners more than one way to examine X.

blocks.title: E2C 课外活动与能力形成
blocks.name: 课外活动与能力形成
blocks.chain: real responsibilities → coordination and feedback → interpersonal skills and resilience
blocks.model: Extracurricular activities can develop abilities that are difficult to practise through individual written work alone. Students organising a school event must divide responsibilities, respond to delays and communicate when plans change. If something goes wrong, they have to adjust their approach and consider how their actions affect the rest of the group. These experiences can strengthen cooperation and resilience because the consequences of their decisions are visible. Simply joining a club is unlikely to produce the same benefits unless students take an active role and have opportunities to reflect on their performance.
blocks.guide: 把参加活动拆成分工、应变与反馈，避免活动名称直接跳到品质。仿写 X develops when learners have to do Y and respond to Z.

topics.description: 在专业深度、知识广度与课外能力之间取舍。

topics.title: E3 Assessment and Rewards 评价与奖励
topics.name: 评价与奖励

blocks.title: E3A 奖励优秀表现
blocks.name: 奖励优秀表现
blocks.chain: clear standards → valued achievement → directed effort → stronger performance
blocks.model: Rewarding high achievement can encourage effort by making the standards of success visible. When students understand which qualities are recognised, such as accurate reasoning or careful analysis, they have a clearer target for improvement. Recognition may also give accomplished learners a reason to continue challenging themselves instead of settling for work that is already easy. This approach is most constructive when the criteria are transparent and attainable through learning. If rewards simply reflect advantages students brought into the classroom, they may do less to encourage effort among the wider group.
blocks.guide: 指明奖励什么表现，并区分努力产生的成绩与原有优势。仿写 Recognition is most constructive when the criteria are X and Y.

blocks.title: E3B 奖励进步
blocks.name: 奖励进步
blocks.chain: improvement recognised → progress feels attainable → confidence in effort → persistence
blocks.model: Recognising improvement can help students remain motivated even when they are far from the highest-performing members of the class. A learner who repeatedly receives low rankings may conclude that additional effort will make little difference. If assessment also acknowledges better organisation or fewer recurring mistakes, the same learner gains evidence that progress is possible. This can make continued practice feel worthwhile. Rewarding improvement therefore broadens participation in success, provided that teachers still maintain clear expectations and help students move towards meaningful standards of competence over time.
blocks.guide: 写出学生如何解读反馈，解释进步奖励为何支持持续努力。仿写 If assessment acknowledges X, learners gain evidence that Y is possible.

blocks.title: E3C 狭窄指标与应试行为
blocks.name: 狭窄指标与应试行为
blocks.chain: narrow measures determine rewards → effort shifts towards measurable outputs → wider learning neglected
blocks.model: Assessment can distort learning when a narrow set of measurable results determines nearly all rewards. Students and teachers may then concentrate on the activities most likely to improve those results, even if other abilities matter just as much. For example, repeated practice of predictable question formats may take time away from discussion or independent investigation. Scores could improve while the ability to apply knowledge remains underdeveloped. A more balanced assessment system should therefore use several forms of evidence, so that success reflects a broader range of worthwhile learning outcomes.
blocks.guide: 指标改变行为，再产生被忽略的能力，不直接断言考试无用。仿写 Scores may improve while the ability to X remains underdeveloped.

topics.description: 用奖励标准解释动力、公平与学习行为。

topics.title: E4 Family School Teachers and Peers 家庭学校教师与同伴
topics.name: 家庭学校教师与同伴

blocks.title: E4A 家庭示范与习惯
blocks.name: 家庭示范与习惯
blocks.chain: repeated examples and routines → expectations internalised → habits and values
blocks.model: Families can exert a lasting influence on children because everyday behaviour is learned through repeated experience. A child who regularly observes adults listening respectfully or keeping promises receives practical examples of how people should treat one another. Consistent routines also make certain actions, such as reading or helping with household tasks, part of ordinary life. Over time, these repeated expectations may become habits that require less external supervision. The influence depends on the quality and consistency of family interaction, and it continues to develop alongside experiences at school and with friends.
blocks.guide: 用重复经验连接环境与习惯，避免早期影响决定一切。仿写 Repeated expectations may become habits that require less X.

blocks.title: E4B 教师反馈与理解
blocks.name: 教师反馈与理解
blocks.chain: misconceptions identified → targeted explanation → revised understanding → more effective learning
blocks.model: Teachers support learning by identifying difficulties that students may be unable to recognise themselves. A learner can repeat an incorrect method many times while believing that the extra practice is useful. By examining the reasoning behind an answer, a teacher can locate the misunderstanding and provide an explanation or task that addresses it directly. The student then has a clearer basis for changing their approach. This kind of feedback makes practice more productive and shows why access to information alone may be insufficient without guidance on how to understand and use it.
blocks.guide: 明确诊断错误这一中间环节，适用于教师与网络资源比较。仿写 By examining X, a teacher can identify Y and provide Z.

blocks.title: E4C 学校与同伴社会化
blocks.name: 学校与同伴社会化
blocks.chain: shared tasks and rules → negotiation and consequences → social competence
blocks.model: School gives children repeated opportunities to learn how to cooperate with people outside their families. In a shared task, students must explain their preferences, listen to competing suggestions and agree on how responsibilities will be divided. They also experience the consequences of failing to contribute or refusing to respect common rules. With appropriate guidance, these situations can develop communication and a sense of responsibility towards others. The social value of school consequently depends partly on how interaction is organised, since an environment that tolerates exclusion may teach very different lessons.
blocks.guide: 展开合作中的具体动作，并承认学校环境可能传递不同规范。仿写 With appropriate guidance, these situations can develop X.

topics.description: 区分家庭示范、教师反馈与同伴互动的影响。

topics.title: E5 Learning Methods 学习方式
topics.name: 学习方式

blocks.title: E5A 独立学习
blocks.name: 独立学习
blocks.chain: pace adjusted to need → focused practice → self-monitoring → greater autonomy
blocks.model: Independent study allows learners to adjust the pace and focus of their work to their own needs. A student who understands one topic quickly can move on, while another can spend longer reviewing a difficult explanation without feeling pressured by a group. Planning this work also requires learners to notice gaps in their understanding and decide how to address them. These decisions can gradually strengthen self-discipline and autonomy. Some guidance remains valuable, particularly for inexperienced students who may lack the knowledge needed to judge whether their chosen methods are effective.
blocks.guide: 从个性化节奏推进到自我监控，结尾限定学习经验。仿写 Planning X requires learners to identify Y and decide how to address it.

blocks.title: E5B 小组学习与理解深化
blocks.name: 小组学习与理解深化
blocks.chain: explanation to peers → gaps exposed → feedback and revision → deeper understanding
blocks.model: Group study can deepen understanding because explaining an idea requires learners to organise their reasoning clearly. A student may feel confident after reading a chapter but discover missing steps when a classmate asks why a conclusion follows. Other group members can then offer alternative explanations or point out assumptions that have been overlooked. This exchange encourages learners to revise their initial understanding instead of merely repeating information. The benefit is strongest when everyone contributes and disagreement is treated as an opportunity to examine ideas more carefully.
blocks.guide: 核心是解释暴露理解缺口，不只写交换观点。仿写 A learner may feel X but discover Y when asked to explain Z.

blocks.title: E5C 小组学习的参与条件
blocks.name: 小组学习的参与条件
blocks.chain: unequal participation → passive reliance → limited individual practice → uneven learning
blocks.model: Group work may produce weak learning outcomes when a few confident students complete most of the task. Quieter members can accept the final answer without testing their own understanding, while the active participants become responsible for work that should have been shared. A successful group product may therefore conceal important differences in what each person has learned. Teachers can reduce this problem by assigning clear responsibilities and asking students to explain their individual contributions. These arrangements make participation more visible and help ensure that cooperation includes genuine intellectual effort from each learner.
blocks.guide: 区分小组成果与个人学习，并用可观察参与对应搭便车问题。仿写 A successful group product may conceal differences in X.

topics.description: 比较独立学习的专注与小组讨论的价值。

topics.title: E6 Online Education 线上教育
topics.name: 线上教育

blocks.title: E6A 降低参与门槛
blocks.name: 降低参与门槛
blocks.chain: travel and scheduling barriers reduced → participation becomes feasible → wider access
blocks.model: Online education can widen access by reducing the practical barriers that prevent some people from attending conventional classes. A working parent, for example, may be unable to travel to a campus at a fixed time but could study a recorded lesson after completing family responsibilities. Flexible delivery allows education to fit around commitments that would otherwise make participation impossible. This can create opportunities for learners who are capable and motivated but constrained by location or time. The advantage concerns access, however, and still needs to be supported by effective teaching and feedback.
blocks.guide: 用一个具体受益者解释门槛下降，再区分参与机会与学习成效。仿写 X allows Y to fit around commitments that would otherwise prevent Z.

blocks.title: E6B 数字条件与学习差距
blocks.name: 数字条件与学习差距
blocks.chain: unequal devices and study support → unequal ability to participate → existing gaps may persist
blocks.model: Expanding online courses will not necessarily make education equally accessible to all learners. Students need a reliable connection, a suitable device and a reasonably quiet place to study before they can benefit from the material. Those sharing one device with several family members may miss discussions or struggle to complete assignments on time. Learners also differ in their ability to organise work without regular supervision. Unless these practical and educational needs are addressed, moving courses online may remove geographical barriers while leaving other sources of inequality largely unchanged.
blocks.guide: 区分被消除的障碍与仍然存在的障碍。仿写 X may remove A while leaving B largely unchanged.

blocks.title: E6C 线上课程的互动设计
blocks.name: 线上课程的互动设计
blocks.chain: structured discussion and feedback → active participation → social connection and learning
blocks.model: The social limitations of online education depend greatly on course design. When students only watch recordings and submit individual assignments, they have few reasons to exchange ideas or form supportive relationships. A course that includes small discussion groups, shared projects and regular feedback creates more opportunities for interaction. Students can question one another and receive recognition for their contributions, even when they are physically separated. These arrangements require time and thoughtful organisation, but they show that reduced social contact is a risk that can be addressed rather than an unavoidable feature of online learning.
blocks.guide: 对照两种课程设计，让因果原因落在教学安排上。仿写 When a course includes X, learners have more opportunities to Y.

topics.description: 分析远程学习的门槛、数字差距与互动设计。

topics.title: E7 Education and Employability 教育与就业能力
topics.name: 教育与就业能力

blocks.title: E7A 真实任务与岗位能力
blocks.name: 真实任务与岗位能力
blocks.chain: authentic tasks → application and feedback → practical competence → easier workplace transition
blocks.model: Practical projects can help students translate academic knowledge into skills that employers can use. In a project with a real deadline and a defined audience, learners must decide which information is relevant, coordinate with others and revise work in response to feedback. These demands resemble the decisions they are likely to face in employment more closely than recalling facts in isolation. Graduates who have practised this process may require less support when entering a workplace. The value of practical learning therefore lies in its connection to meaningful tasks and informed feedback.
blocks.guide: 解释真实任务与工作的相似要求，不只列实习等措施。仿写 These demands resemble X more closely than Y does.

blocks.title: E7B 理论与实践脱节
blocks.name: 理论与实践脱节
blocks.chain: limited application → knowledge remains difficult to transfer → mismatch with workplace demands
blocks.model: Graduates may struggle at work when their education provides extensive theoretical knowledge but little opportunity to apply it. Knowing the definition of a communication strategy, for example, does not ensure that a new employee can explain a difficult decision to a dissatisfied client. Such situations require judgement, adaptation and practice with feedback. Employers may therefore perceive a skills gap even among applicants with strong academic results. However, this explains only part of the employment problem, since a shortage of suitable vacancies can prevent well-prepared graduates from finding work too.
blocks.guide: 用知道概念与实际完成任务的差别解释技能缺口，并保留需求因素。仿写 Knowing X does not ensure that a person can Y.

topics.description: 解释课程知识怎样转化为真实岗位能力。

topics.title: E8 Child Development and Behaviour 儿童发展与行为迁移
topics.name: 儿童发展与行为迁移

blocks.title: E8A 儿童屏幕习惯的迁移段
blocks.name: 儿童屏幕习惯的迁移段
blocks.chain: repeated displacement of conversation → fewer communication opportunities → narrower practice
blocks.model: The effect of children's screen habits should be considered in relation to the experiences they replace. If a child routinely watches videos during family meals, there is less opportunity to describe events, listen to other people and respond to questions. These ordinary exchanges give children repeated practice in communication. Replacing them occasionally is different from removing them from the daily routine altogether. Parents can therefore make more informed decisions by considering when screens are used and whether children still have regular opportunities for active conversation and shared activities.
blocks.guide: 将 T3 的替代机制迁移到具体儿童发展场景；改变的是被替代活动及其功能。

blocks.title: E8B 多方共同影响行为
blocks.name: 多方共同影响行为
blocks.chain: consistent expectations across settings → repeated reinforcement → more stable behaviour
blocks.model: Children's behaviour is shaped by the combined messages they receive at home, at school and from friends. Expectations are easier to understand when these environments reinforce similar standards, such as resolving disagreements without aggression. A child who practises this response in several settings has repeated opportunities to see how it works. Conflicting messages, by contrast, may make acceptable behaviour less clear. Cooperation between families and schools can therefore strengthen guidance, while still recognising that children gradually develop their own judgement and respond differently to similar experiences.
blocks.guide: 将 E4 各影响源连接起来，解释一致性如何发挥作用。

blocks.title: E8C 教育与青少年犯罪预防
blocks.name: 教育与青少年犯罪预防
blocks.chain: sustained engagement and support → attainable legitimate goals → reduced attraction of harmful groups
blocks.model: Education can contribute to crime prevention by giving vulnerable young people a stronger connection to legitimate opportunities. A student who receives practical guidance and succeeds in a meaningful task may begin to see an achievable route into further training or work. Supportive adults can also notice disengagement early and help address difficulties before they become more serious. These experiences may reduce the appeal of groups that offer belonging through harmful behaviour. Educational support is therefore most useful when it is combined with attention to the young person's wider family and social circumstances.
blocks.guide: 将 C5 的干预逻辑迁移到学校，说明教育改变了什么选择与联系。

topics.description: 将屏幕习惯、共同引导与犯罪预防迁移到儿童发展。

topics.title: W1 Teamwork and Competition 团队合作与竞争
topics.name: 团队合作与竞争

blocks.title: W1A 互补能力与复杂任务
blocks.name: 互补能力与复杂任务
blocks.chain: complementary knowledge shared → blind spots reduced → better decisions on complex tasks
blocks.model: Teamwork can improve performance when a problem requires knowledge that no single employee possesses. One member may understand technical constraints, while another knows how customers are likely to respond. Sharing these perspectives allows the group to identify weaknesses before committing to a decision. It also makes it possible to divide tasks according to relevant strengths. The benefit depends on open communication, since merely placing people in the same team does not ensure that their knowledge will be combined. Cooperation is particularly valuable when the parts of a task are closely connected.
blocks.guide: 明确成员贡献了哪些不同信息，再解释信息组合的价值。仿写 One person may understand X, while another knows Y.

blocks.title: W1B 公平竞争与努力
blocks.name: 公平竞争与努力
blocks.chain: credible rewards and clear rules → effort appears worthwhile → stronger performance
blocks.model: Competition can encourage effort when employees believe that success depends on work they can improve. Clear criteria give people a reason to develop useful skills, and a credible reward makes the additional effort worthwhile. A sales team, for instance, may work harder to understand customer needs when good performance is recognised fairly. However, the criteria must reflect the organisation's broader interests. If only short-term sales are rewarded, staff may neglect customer trust. Constructive competition therefore requires rules that connect individual achievement with outcomes the organisation actually values.
blocks.guide: 奖励改变努力方向，因此必须说明衡量什么。仿写 Competition is constructive when rewards connect X with Y.

blocks.title: W1C 内部竞争与信息保留
blocks.name: 内部竞争与信息保留
blocks.chain: colleagues treated as rivals → information withheld → coordination weakened → collective losses
blocks.model: Excessive competition inside an organisation can undermine the cooperation that many tasks require. If employees gain an advantage whenever a colleague performs poorly, sharing useful information may appear contrary to their own interests. Staff may then protect contacts, delay assistance or avoid admitting mistakes. These behaviours make it harder for the organisation to learn and coordinate its work. Individual performance figures could remain impressive while the overall service deteriorates. Employers should therefore consider whether their reward systems encourage employees to contribute to shared goals as well as pursue personal success.
blocks.guide: 用利益结构解释为何不合作，避免笼统说竞争使人自私。仿写 If people benefit when X, doing Y may appear contrary to their interests.

topics.description: 比较团队互补、公平竞争与过度竞争的代价。

topics.title: W2 Recruitment 招聘与能力判断
topics.name: 招聘与能力判断

blocks.title: W2A 学历的筛选作用
blocks.name: 学历的筛选作用
blocks.chain: recognised qualifications → evidence of prior study → manageable screening → limits require additional evidence
blocks.model: Academic qualifications can provide employers with a practical starting point when evaluating many applicants. Completing a relevant course suggests that a candidate has encountered essential concepts and met a recognised standard of assessment. This information is useful when employers cannot investigate every applicant's background in detail. Nevertheless, qualifications reveal only part of what a person can do. Courses differ, and success in formal assessment may not demonstrate the ability to handle unfamiliar workplace demands. Employers can therefore use qualifications as an initial indicator while seeking further evidence of practical competence.
blocks.guide: 承认筛选成本，再限定学历证据的范围。仿写 X provides a starting point, while further evidence is needed to assess Y.

blocks.title: W2B 工作样本与实际表现
blocks.name: 工作样本与实际表现
blocks.chain: relevant task performed → skills become observable → better evidence for selection
blocks.model: Work samples can make recruitment more informative by showing how candidates approach tasks similar to those required in the role. An applicant for an editing position, for example, could be asked to improve a short passage and explain the changes. Employers would then see evidence of judgement and accuracy rather than relying entirely on confident claims in an interview. The task should be reasonably brief and directly relevant to the vacancy. Otherwise, the process may burden applicants without providing a fair or useful indication of their likely performance.
blocks.guide: 用岗位对应的任务证明能力可观察，同时考虑测试成本与公平性。仿写 X allows employers to observe Y rather than rely entirely on claims about Z.

blocks.title: W2C 结构化面试与公平比较
blocks.name: 结构化面试与公平比较
blocks.chain: comparable questions and criteria → less reliance on impressions → more consistent evaluation
blocks.model: Interviews are more useful when they examine relevant judgement through comparable questions. Asking each candidate how they would respond to the same workplace difficulty gives employers a clearer basis for evaluating their reasoning. Agreed criteria can also reduce the influence of confidence, personal similarity or an unusually engaging conversation. This does not eliminate uncertainty, since a well-expressed answer is still different from performance under real pressure. However, combining a structured interview with other relevant evidence can make recruitment more consistent and help employers avoid decisions based mainly on first impressions.
blocks.guide: 解释标准化为何提高可比性，再承认口头回答的边界。仿写 Agreed criteria can reduce the influence of X on decisions about Y.

topics.description: 从学历、工作样本和面试识别实际能力。

topics.title: W3 Leadership 领导力
topics.name: 领导力

blocks.title: W3A 明确方向与集中决策
blocks.name: 明确方向与集中决策
blocks.chain: clear priorities and authority → uncertainty reduced → coordinated action under time pressure
blocks.model: Effective leadership can improve performance by making priorities clear when employees face competing demands. Without a shared direction, different team members may make reasonable individual decisions that conflict with one another. A leader who explains the goal and assigns responsibilities helps people coordinate their efforts. Concentrated authority may be particularly useful during an urgent disruption, when lengthy consultation would delay action. Its value depends on informed judgement and clear communication, however, because a rapid decision can still be harmful if the leader misunderstands the situation or ignores essential information.
blocks.guide: 用个人决策之间的冲突解释协调价值，限定集中决策的情境。仿写 Without a shared direction, individual decisions may conflict with one another.

blocks.title: W3B 参与决策与执行意愿
blocks.name: 参与决策与执行意愿
blocks.chain: employees contribute information → decisions improve → understanding and commitment increase
blocks.model: Participatory leadership can be valuable when employees possess information that managers cannot easily obtain on their own. Staff dealing directly with customers or equipment may notice practical difficulties that are invisible in a summary report. Inviting their input allows a decision to reflect these conditions and gives employees a clearer understanding of why a particular approach is chosen. They may consequently be more willing to support its implementation. Consultation works best when its purpose and limits are clear, so that gathering useful contributions does not prevent a timely final decision.
blocks.guide: 同时展开信息质量与参与意愿，两者连接同一个决策过程。仿写 Inviting input allows a decision to reflect X and gives people Y.

topics.description: 比较集中决策与成员参与的适用条件。

topics.title: W4 Salary Satisfaction and Meaning 薪资满意度与工作意义
topics.name: 薪资满意度与工作意义

blocks.title: W4A 收入与基本安全
blocks.name: 收入与基本安全
blocks.chain: dependable income → essential expenses covered → uncertainty reduced → greater security
blocks.model: Salary is an important consideration because employment must enable people to meet ordinary financial responsibilities. A reliable income allows workers to pay for housing, support dependants and prepare for unexpected expenses. When these needs are insecure, even an interesting job may become a source of persistent worry. Higher pay can therefore make a substantial difference for someone whose current earnings are insufficient. The importance of additional income may change as circumstances improve, however, making it necessary to consider working conditions and personal priorities alongside the size of the salary.
blocks.guide: 先写薪资解决的具体问题，再限定其重要性随处境变化。仿写 X can make a substantial difference when Y remains insecure.

blocks.title: W4B 工作与身份意义
blocks.name: 工作与身份意义
blocks.chain: autonomy and useful contribution → competence and purpose → greater satisfaction
blocks.model: Work can provide a sense of purpose when people feel that their abilities are being used in a worthwhile way. Completing a difficult task or helping a client can give employees evidence of competence and contribution. Some control over how the work is done may strengthen this feeling by allowing them to exercise judgement rather than simply follow instructions. These experiences can make a career personally meaningful. Their importance varies between individuals, and a fulfilling life may also draw heavily on relationships, interests and responsibilities outside paid employment.
blocks.guide: 把意义落实为能力感、贡献感和自主判断，回应工作是否最重要时保留其他来源。

blocks.title: W4C 工作要求与精疲力竭
blocks.name: 工作要求与精疲力竭
blocks.chain: excessive demands → recovery and family time reduced → exhaustion and strained relationships
blocks.model: A demanding career can reduce well-being when professional responsibilities consistently consume the time needed for recovery and personal relationships. Employees who remain available late into the evening may find it difficult to rest or participate fully in family life. Over time, tiredness and unresolved responsibilities can make both work and home more stressful. A higher salary may compensate for some inconvenience, but it cannot restore every lost opportunity for rest or connection. Career decisions should therefore consider whether the demands of a position are sustainable alongside other important parts of life.
blocks.guide: 解释压力通过时间与恢复不足累积，避免薪资高必然不幸福。仿写 The demands of X should be considered alongside the time required for Y.

topics.description: 收入保障、工作意义与过度要求的长期影响。

topics.title: W5 Parental Leave 育儿假
topics.name: 育儿假

blocks.title: W5A 父亲参与与照护分担
blocks.name: 父亲参与与照护分担
blocks.chain: time available for care → practical skills and routines → more balanced responsibilities
blocks.model: Parental leave for fathers can support a more equal division of childcare by giving them time to develop practical experience. Regularly feeding, comforting and organising care for a child helps a parent become familiar with needs that cannot be understood through occasional assistance alone. These routines may make it easier for both parents to continue sharing responsibilities after the leave ends. Mothers may then have greater freedom to recover or return to other activities. The benefit is stronger when fathers are genuinely able and encouraged to use the leave for caregiving.
blocks.guide: 时间不是直接等于平等；补出照护经验和习惯形成。仿写 Regular participation in X helps people develop Y, making Z more feasible.

blocks.title: W5B 休假与企业成本
blocks.name: 休假与企业成本
blocks.chain: temporary absence → tasks reassigned or replacement recruited → coordination and financial costs
blocks.model: Parental leave can create practical difficulties for employers, particularly where a small team depends on specialised staff. During an employee's absence, colleagues may need to absorb additional work or the business may have to recruit and train a temporary replacement. These adjustments carry costs even when the employer supports the purpose of the policy. The burden depends on how much notice is available and how leave is funded. Shared funding arrangements and predictable planning can make it easier to protect family welfare while maintaining the continuity of essential business activities.
blocks.guide: 指出小企业为何更敏感，再让资金安排和提前规划分别回应成本来源。

topics.description: 权衡照护分担与企业的人员安排成本。

topics.title: W6 Income Disparity and Executive Pay 收入差距与高管薪酬
topics.name: 收入差距与高管薪酬

blocks.title: W6A 薪资与稀缺能力
blocks.name: 薪资与稀缺能力
blocks.chain: compensation reflects difficult responsibilities → suitable candidates attracted → incentive to perform
blocks.model: Differences in pay can be justified when roles require scarce abilities or carry substantial responsibilities. An organisation may need to offer competitive compensation to attract someone capable of managing decisions that affect many employees and customers. Appropriate rewards can also give capable staff a reason to develop the expertise needed for demanding positions. However, this argument depends on a credible relationship between compensation and contribution. A large salary by itself does not demonstrate that the recipient creates comparable value, so the basis on which rewards are determined matters greatly.
blocks.guide: 将薪酬差异的正当性落在能力与责任，并检验贡献证据。仿写 This argument depends on a credible relationship between X and Y.

blocks.title: W6B 不公平感与组织信任
blocks.name: 不公平感与组织信任
blocks.chain: rewards appear detached from contribution → fairness questioned → trust and commitment weakened
blocks.model: Large pay differences may damage trust when employees cannot see how they relate to responsibility or performance. If senior managers receive generous rewards while ordinary staff face stagnant wages despite contributing to success, workers may question whether the organisation values them fairly. This perception can reduce willingness to offer additional effort or support difficult changes. The concern is particularly strong when poor decisions seem to carry few consequences for those at the top. Transparent reward criteria can help address these doubts, although explanations must be consistent with actual treatment.
blocks.guide: 收入差距通过公平感影响信任，而不是差距本身必然导致冲突。

topics.description: 解释稀缺能力、薪酬差距与组织信任。

topics.title: W7 Automation and Employment 职业变化迁移
topics.name: 职业变化迁移

blocks.title: W7A 入门岗位与经验积累
blocks.name: 入门岗位与经验积累
blocks.chain: routine entry tasks automated → fewer chances to practise → progression routes need redesign
blocks.model: Automation may affect career development even when it does not eliminate an entire profession. Junior employees often gain experience through relatively routine tasks before taking responsibility for difficult decisions. If these initial tasks are transferred to software, organisations may offer fewer opportunities for newcomers to develop practical judgement. Experienced workers could remain valuable while access to the profession becomes harder for graduates. Employers may therefore need to redesign training, using supervised projects and feedback to replace the learning opportunities previously provided by routine entry-level work.
blocks.guide: 从 T1 迁移到职业阶梯，解释入门任务同时承担培训功能。

blocks.title: W7B 持续培训与岗位转型
blocks.name: 持续培训与岗位转型
blocks.chain: new task requirements identified → accessible training and practice → workers move into complementary roles
blocks.model: Retraining is more useful when it is closely connected to the tasks that are actually expanding. Offering employees a general course may have little value if they cannot practise the new skills or find roles that require them. A stronger approach combines instruction with supervised work on relevant projects, allowing staff to build competence before taking on full responsibility. Employers can also provide time to learn so that participation does not depend entirely on personal savings. These conditions make it more realistic for existing workers to move into roles that complement new technology.
blocks.guide: 将再培训拆成岗位相关性、实践和时间支持，避免把措施名称当作解释。

topics.description: 理解入门机会、经验积累与持续培训。

topics.title: G1 Public Funding 公共资金
topics.name: 公共资金

blocks.title: G1A 机会成本与项目比较
blocks.name: 机会成本与项目比较
blocks.chain: limited budget → one programme funded → alternatives forgone → comparison of public value
blocks.model: Public spending involves opportunity costs because governments cannot fund every worthwhile proposal to the same extent. Resources committed to a new cultural venue, for example, are unavailable for other projects within the same budget. The relevant question is therefore how much additional public benefit each option would produce. A venue serving an area with few cultural facilities may have a stronger case than another venue in a well-served district. Comparing need, likely use and ongoing costs allows governments to explain their priorities more convincingly than simply declaring one category of spending universally important.
blocks.guide: 比较具体新增项目的收益，而非把整个支出类别永久排序。仿写 The relevant question is how much additional benefit each option would produce.

blocks.title: G1B 长期投入与持续收益
blocks.name: 长期投入与持续收益
blocks.chain: early investment → future capacity improved → recurring benefits → present spending may be justified
blocks.model: Some public investments deserve support even when their benefits are not immediate. Improving education or maintaining transport infrastructure can increase the capacity of a community to function effectively for many years. Better preparation may help future workers perform more demanding tasks, while reliable connections can support repeated journeys to jobs and services. These continuing benefits should be considered alongside the initial expense. However, the existence of a possible long-term benefit is not sufficient on its own; governments still need a plausible explanation of how the investment will be used and maintained.
blocks.guide: 写出未来收益如何持续出现，并保留使用与维护条件。

topics.description: 比较有限预算中的紧迫需求和长期收益。

topics.title: G2 Public and Private Provision 公共与私人供给
topics.name: 公共与私人供给

blocks.title: G2A 市场供给不足与公共支持
blocks.name: 市场供给不足与公共支持
blocks.chain: benefits cannot be fully captured by providers → weak commercial incentive → public support expands provision
blocks.model: Public support is particularly valuable when an activity benefits people beyond those who directly pay for it. A research project, for instance, may generate knowledge that other organisations can use, making it difficult for the original funder to capture all the resulting value. A commercial provider may consequently invest less than would be desirable from society's perspective. Government funding can help address this gap. A separate argument concerns affordability: subsidies may allow people with limited incomes to use essential services even when they cannot meet the full price themselves.
blocks.guide: 将外溢收益导致的市场供给不足与支付能力不足的公平问题分清。

blocks.title: G2B 竞争与服务效率
blocks.name: 竞争与服务效率
blocks.chain: users can compare and switch → providers face pressure → service or efficiency may improve
blocks.model: Private providers may improve services when customers can compare alternatives and move to a better option. The risk of losing users creates an incentive to respond to complaints, control avoidable costs and develop more convenient ways of delivering the service. These pressures can benefit consumers without requiring the government to manage every operational decision. However, the mechanism weakens when users lack reliable information or have no realistic alternative provider. Effective competition therefore depends on the structure of the market, making regulation and public purchasing arrangements important alongside private ownership.
blocks.guide: 明确比较与退出的条件，避免私人所有制直接等于效率。

topics.description: 权衡普遍可及、市场效率与公共支持。

topics.title: G3 Taxation and Welfare 税收与福利
topics.name: 税收与福利

blocks.title: G3A 再分配与机会
blocks.name: 再分配与机会
blocks.chain: tax revenue → essential services and protection → barriers reduced → greater opportunity
blocks.model: Tax-funded services can improve equality of opportunity by reducing the importance of family income in access to essential support. A child whose household cannot afford private tuition may still benefit from a well-resourced public school. Similarly, temporary income protection can allow an unemployed adult to search for suitable work without immediately losing the means to meet basic needs. These forms of support can make future participation more realistic. Their value depends on effective delivery and appropriate targeting, since collecting revenue alone does not ensure that assistance reaches people who need it.
blocks.guide: 用教育或失业支持解释机会扩大，区分机会公平与结果相同。

blocks.title: G3B 税收设计与工作激励
blocks.name: 税收设计与工作激励
blocks.chain: extra earnings largely offset → limited gain from additional work → incentives may weaken
blocks.model: Taxes and welfare rules can weaken work incentives if additional earnings produce very little improvement in a person's disposable income. This may happen when higher wages are taxed while existing benefits are withdrawn at the same time. Someone considering extra working hours could then face substantial childcare or travel costs for only a small financial gain. The problem concerns the combined design of the system rather than taxation in the abstract. Gradual benefit withdrawal and attention to participation costs can help preserve financial protection while making additional work more worthwhile.
blocks.guide: 用到手收入的变化解释激励，不使用税高所以懒惰的跳步。

topics.description: 把税收与福利连接到机会和工作激励。

topics.title: G4 Regulation Taxes and Bans 监管税收与禁令
topics.name: 监管税收与禁令

blocks.title: G4A 社会成本与激励调整
blocks.name: 社会成本与激励调整
blocks.chain: private choices impose public costs → incentives adjusted → harmful behaviour becomes less attractive
blocks.model: Regulation can be justified when the cost of an activity is partly borne by people who did not choose it. A business that pollutes a shared environment may otherwise have little financial reason to reduce the harm, since affected residents carry much of the burden. Standards or charges can make that harm relevant to the business's own decisions. If cleaner methods are available, the firm then has a stronger reason to adopt them. The effectiveness of the policy depends on credible enforcement and on whether the rules target the actual source of the damage.
blocks.guide: 分清行为者与承担成本者，再说明政策改变了谁的选择。

blocks.title: G4B 政策副作用与替代选择
blocks.name: 政策副作用与替代选择
blocks.chain: restrictions without feasible alternatives → avoidance or unequal burdens → weaker policy outcomes
blocks.model: A restriction may produce disappointing results if it ignores the alternatives available to those affected. Charging people to use cars, for example, can create pressure to change behaviour, but residents without reliable public transport may have little practical choice. They could simply pay more while continuing the same journeys. The burden may fall especially heavily on people with inflexible work schedules. A stronger policy would combine incentives with usable alternatives and assess who bears the costs, so that the intervention creates a realistic route towards the behaviour it is intended to encourage.
blocks.guide: 从缺少替代项解释政策为什么失效，并让配套措施回应这一原因。

topics.description: 评估税收、标准、禁令与可行替代的效果。

topics.title: G5 Shared Responsibility 共同责任
topics.name: 共同责任

blocks.title: G5A 政府塑造可行选择
blocks.name: 政府塑造可行选择
blocks.chain: infrastructure and information → feasible alternatives → individual action becomes easier
blocks.model: Governments influence behaviour by shaping the options that people can realistically use. Encouraging residents to travel sustainably will have limited effect if neighbourhoods lack safe walking routes or dependable public transport. Providing these facilities changes the practical decision people face by reducing the inconvenience of an alternative journey. Information can then help residents make use of the new options. Public responsibility therefore includes creating conditions in which desirable choices are achievable, particularly when individuals cannot coordinate or finance the necessary infrastructure on their own.
blocks.guide: 写出设施改变的是选择成本与可行性，适用于环保、运动和交通。

blocks.title: G5B 个人在可行范围内负责
blocks.name: 个人在可行范围内负责
blocks.chain: usable options exist → repeated personal decisions → collective outcomes
blocks.model: Individuals retain an important role once they have access to reasonable information and practical alternatives. A well-designed recycling system, for instance, still depends on residents sorting their household waste appropriately. If many people ignore the available facilities, the public investment cannot achieve its intended result. Personal responsibility therefore involves acting on opportunities that are genuinely available, while recognising that constraints differ between households. This approach avoids expecting individuals to solve structural problems alone, but also acknowledges that institutions cannot substitute for every everyday decision.
blocks.guide: 区分能够选择却不行动与缺乏条件，避免责任论证一刀切。

blocks.title: G5C 企业对产品与营销负责
blocks.name: 企业对产品与营销负责
blocks.chain: product and marketing decisions shape options → consumer behaviour influenced → business responsibility
blocks.model: Businesses share responsibility for social outcomes because they influence what consumers are offered and how those options are presented. A product that is difficult to repair may encourage replacement even when the owner would prefer to keep using it. Similarly, unclear marketing can make it harder for customers to assess the consequences of a purchase. Firms can address these problems through more transparent information and designs that support responsible use. Their influence means that debates about behaviour should consider commercial practices alongside government policy and individual choices.
blocks.guide: 说明消费者选择之前，企业已经决定了哪些条件。

topics.description: 区分政府、个人和企业能够承担的责任。

topics.title: G6 Transport and Urban Infrastructure 交通与城市基础设施
topics.name: 交通与城市基础设施

blocks.title: G6A 公共交通与驾车替代
blocks.name: 公共交通与驾车替代
blocks.chain: reliable and convenient transit → driving becomes less necessary → traffic pressure may decline
blocks.model: Investment in public transport can reduce car dependence when it creates a realistic alternative for everyday journeys. Commuters are more likely to leave their cars at home if services arrive regularly, connect with their destinations and do not impose excessive waiting time. These improvements reduce the practical advantages of driving. If enough existing drivers change modes, pressure on busy roads may ease. The outcome therefore depends on service quality and actual changes in travel behaviour, rather than simply on the number of buses or stations a city purchases.
blocks.guide: 补出原有驾车者换乘这一环，区分设施数量与实际效果。

blocks.title: G6B 交通连接与机会
blocks.name: 交通连接与机会
blocks.chain: better connections → more destinations reachable → access to jobs and services
blocks.model: Transport infrastructure can improve living standards by increasing the range of opportunities people can reach. A job may be unsuitable for a qualified applicant if travelling to it is too expensive or takes several hours each day. Better connections can make that same vacancy practical without requiring the person to move home. Access to education and healthcare may improve through the same mechanism. The economic value of a transport project should therefore include the opportunities it opens up, especially for communities that previously had limited access to essential destinations.
blocks.guide: 以岗位存在但无法到达说明可达性，适用于城乡差距。

blocks.title: G6C 道路扩建与新增需求
blocks.name: 道路扩建与新增需求
blocks.chain: driving becomes easier → more journeys or longer commutes → congestion relief may diminish
blocks.model: Building additional roads may offer only temporary relief if easier driving encourages more people to use cars. Shorter journey times can make previously inconvenient trips attractive or allow households to live farther from their workplaces. As these decisions accumulate, part of the new road capacity may be absorbed by additional traffic. This does not mean that every road project lacks value, especially where essential connections are missing. It means that congestion policy should consider changes in demand and land use as well as the amount of road space provided.
blocks.guide: 解释便利如何反过来增加需求，避免把扩路效果写成固定结论。

topics.description: 从出行选择、可达性与新增需求分析交通投入。

topics.title: G7 Opportunity Cost 机会成本迁移
topics.name: 机会成本迁移

blocks.title: G7A 时间预算与个人取舍
blocks.name: 时间预算与个人取舍
blocks.chain: limited time → one activity expanded → another reduced → comparison of forgone benefits
blocks.model: Opportunity cost also matters when individuals decide how to use their time. A student who adds several hours of paid work each week may gain useful income and experience, but those hours must come from study, rest or other commitments. The decision is sensible only when the benefits are considered alongside what is being given up. The same number of working hours can therefore have different consequences for students with different workloads or financial needs. Evaluating the alternative use of time makes the reasoning more precise than assuming that an activity is always beneficial.
blocks.guide: 将 G1 的资金取舍迁移到时间，明确被放弃的具体活动与收益。

topics.description: 将机会成本迁移到个人的时间与资源分配。

topics.title: G8 Major Sporting Events 大型体育赛事
topics.name: 大型体育赛事

blocks.title: G8A 赛事投资与持续使用
blocks.name: 赛事投资与持续使用
blocks.chain: event prompts useful investment → facilities serve later needs → benefits extend beyond the event
blocks.model: Hosting a major sporting event can leave lasting benefits when investment is connected to the city's existing needs. Transport improvements made for visitors may later support ordinary commuters, while suitably designed venues can serve local clubs and schools. In this case, the event provides a deadline and an incentive to complete projects that remain useful after international attention has moved elsewhere. The strongest argument for hosting therefore concerns additional value that continues over time. It depends on realistic plans for future use and on whether the same benefits could be achieved more economically through other means.
blocks.guide: 将遗产效应落实为赛后使用者，并加入替代方案比较。

blocks.title: G8B 闲置场馆与长期成本
blocks.name: 闲置场馆与长期成本
blocks.chain: demand overestimated → facilities underused → continuing maintenance costs → pressure on public funds
blocks.model: Large sporting events can create a financial burden when facilities are designed for exceptional demand that does not continue afterwards. A stadium may attract full crowds during the event but lack enough regular users to cover its ongoing costs. Local authorities can then be left paying for maintenance while other services compete for the same funds. Visitor spending during a few weeks may be insufficient to justify these commitments. Careful evaluation should therefore include the full period of ownership and the realistic demand for each facility, rather than focusing mainly on the spectacle of hosting.
blocks.guide: 将一次性收入与持续成本放在同一时间范围内比较。

topics.description: 比较赛事收益、后续利用和场馆维护成本。

topics.title: C1 Punishment and Rehabilitation 惩罚与改造
topics.name: 惩罚与改造

blocks.title: C1A 执法可信度与威慑
blocks.name: 执法可信度与威慑
blocks.chain: credible detection and consequences → perceived risk increases → some offending becomes less attractive
blocks.model: Punishment can discourage some offences when people believe that unlawful behaviour is likely to be detected and followed by meaningful consequences. A potential offender weighing a financial gain against a credible penalty may decide that the risk is not worthwhile. This argument depends on the perceived effectiveness of enforcement, since a severe punishment may have little influence if people expect to avoid detection. It also applies more readily to deliberate decisions than to every form of impulsive behaviour. Deterrence is therefore one useful function of criminal justice, with practical limits that policy should recognise.
blocks.guide: 补出被发现的主观概率，避免刑罚越重效果必然越好。仿写 X may have little influence if people expect Y.

blocks.title: C1B 监禁与即时公共保护
blocks.name: 监禁与即时公共保护
blocks.chain: dangerous offender confined → immediate access to potential victims restricted → temporary protection
blocks.model: Imprisonment can protect the public by limiting a dangerous offender's ability to harm people outside the prison. Where a person presents a continuing and serious threat, this immediate protective function may be difficult to achieve through a lighter response alone. The argument concerns safety during the period of confinement. It does not establish that imprisonment will resolve the factors that contributed to the offence or prevent further harm after release. Decisions about custody should therefore consider the level of risk and the preparation needed for an eventual return to the community.
blocks.guide: 区分关押期间的限制作用与出狱后的长期结果。

blocks.title: C1C 改造与重新融入
blocks.name: 改造与重新融入
blocks.chain: underlying barriers addressed → lawful alternatives become achievable → reintegration → lower reoffending risk
blocks.model: Rehabilitation aims to reduce reoffending by making a lawful life more achievable after release. Someone who leaves prison without usable skills, support or stable accommodation may face many of the same pressures as before. Education, practical preparation and help with personal difficulties can improve the options available at this transition. For example, a person who can obtain regular work has a more realistic source of lawful income and a daily routine to maintain. The benefit depends on support continuing beyond the prison gate, where these newly developed abilities must be put into practice.
blocks.guide: 解释改造改变的是可行选择，并把出狱衔接纳入链条。

topics.description: 区分威慑、即时保护和降低再犯的不同作用。

topics.title: C2 Causes of Crime 犯罪成因
topics.name: 犯罪成因

blocks.title: C2A 排斥与合法机会不足
blocks.name: 排斥与合法机会不足
blocks.chain: exclusion and limited opportunities → legitimate routes appear less accessible → some crime becomes more attractive
blocks.model: Social exclusion may contribute to certain offences by restricting the legitimate opportunities people believe are available to them. A person repeatedly unable to obtain work or training may find it harder to see a realistic route towards financial stability. In that situation, an illegal source of income can appear more attractive than it otherwise would. This is a possible explanation of risk, rather than a prediction about every individual facing hardship. Crime prevention can address these conditions through accessible opportunities while still recognising that people respond differently and remain responsible for their actions.
blocks.guide: 用风险机制而非群体标签；明确只能解释部分犯罪。

blocks.title: C2B 白领犯罪与监督缺口
blocks.name: 白领犯罪与监督缺口
blocks.chain: access to valuable resources + weak oversight → opportunity for personal gain → misconduct risk
blocks.model: Education and financial security do not remove every incentive to commit a crime. A well-qualified employee may have access to funds or confidential information that can be misused for personal gain. If oversight is weak and responsibility is unclear, the opportunity may appear easy to exploit. This helps explain why some offences occur among people who have substantial legitimate opportunities. Measures that focus only on poverty or basic education will therefore be incomplete. Clear accountability, independent checks and effective enforcement are also needed where positions of trust create opportunities for abuse.
blocks.guide: 用反例限定单一成因，并提出针对权限与监督的措施。

topics.description: 从合法机会与监督缺口解释不同犯罪。

topics.title: C3 Education Employment and Reintegration 教育就业与重新融入
topics.name: 教育就业与重新融入

blocks.title: C3A 技能资格与合法收入
blocks.name: 技能资格与合法收入
blocks.chain: relevant prison education → recognised competence → access to work → more stable reintegration
blocks.model: Education in prison can support reintegration when it equips people with skills that employers can recognise and use. Literacy may help someone complete an application, while relevant vocational training can demonstrate the ability to perform a practical task. These improvements make employment more attainable for people previously excluded by a lack of qualifications. Regular work can then provide income, structure and contact with people outside offending networks. The chain is strongest when training reflects available jobs and former prisoners receive realistic assistance with the process of entering employment.
blocks.guide: 将资格、求职过程和工作提供的支持分层展开，适用于教育减刑再犯题。

blocks.title: C3B 教育措施的边界
blocks.name: 教育措施的边界
blocks.chain: skills improve but other barriers remain → work or stability still inaccessible → education alone insufficient
blocks.model: Education alone may have limited influence when the main barriers to reintegration lie elsewhere. A person can complete a useful qualification yet struggle to find work if employers refuse to consider applicants with a criminal record. Unstable accommodation or unresolved personal difficulties may also prevent reliable attendance. These obstacles interrupt the connection between learning and a sustainable lawful life. Education should therefore be combined with practical assistance and appropriate support, rather than being treated as a complete solution. Its value is better understood as one part of a wider process of rebuilding stability.
blocks.guide: 精准指出因果链在哪一环被阻断，比泛泛说原因很多更充分。

topics.description: 连接教育、就业与释放后的持续支持。

topics.title: C4 Technology and Crime Prevention 科技与犯罪预防
topics.name: 科技与犯罪预防

blocks.title: C4A 数字证据与调查效率
blocks.name: 数字证据与调查效率
blocks.chain: relevant records available → events reconstructed → suspects or explanations checked → stronger investigation
blocks.model: Technology can assist crime prevention and investigation by making relevant evidence easier to obtain. A clear recording may help establish what happened in a public place, while a reliable digital record can allow investigators to check conflicting accounts. This can reduce the time spent pursuing an inaccurate explanation and improve the chances of identifying the responsible person. Awareness that such evidence exists may also discourage some deliberate offences. These benefits depend on the quality of the information and careful interpretation, since collecting more data does not ensure that every conclusion drawn from it is correct.
blocks.guide: 说明记录如何改善调查过程，并区分资料数量与判断准确度。

blocks.title: C4B 监控错误与隐私
blocks.name: 监控错误与隐私
blocks.chain: broad monitoring or inaccurate identification → innocent people affected → trust and rights harmed
blocks.model: Crime prevention technology can create problems when monitoring becomes excessively broad or its conclusions are treated as unquestionable. An inaccurate identification may expose an innocent person to investigation, while retaining detailed records of ordinary activities can reveal information unrelated to any offence. People may then lose confidence in institutions that appear unable to justify or correct their use of data. Safeguards should therefore include limits on collection, clear responsibility for decisions and a way to challenge errors. These protections help connect the use of technology to a specific and defensible public purpose.
blocks.guide: 将隐私风险具体化为无关信息收集和错误后果，再配置对应保障。

topics.description: 比较数字证据的作用与监控错误、隐私风险。

topics.title: C5 Youth Crime and Parents 青少年犯罪与父母责任
topics.name: 青少年犯罪与父母责任

blocks.title: C5A 引导与早期干预
blocks.name: 引导与早期干预
blocks.chain: consistent guidance and attention → difficulties noticed early → support and clearer boundaries
blocks.model: Parents can help prevent harmful behaviour by providing consistent guidance and paying attention to changes in a child's daily life. Clear expectations make acceptable conduct easier to understand, while regular conversation may reveal difficulties at school or pressure from friends. These signs give adults an opportunity to offer support before problems become more serious. Schools and community services can reinforce this process when families need additional assistance. Prevention is therefore more realistic when adults have both the capacity to maintain boundaries and the resources to respond constructively to the reasons behind a young person's behaviour.
blocks.guide: 同时解释规则和支持的作用，避免只把监督写成控制。

blocks.title: C5B 父母责任的合理边界
blocks.name: 父母责任的合理边界
blocks.chain: young person's independent agency and wider influences → parental control limited → accountability must be proportionate
blocks.model: Holding parents responsible for every offence committed by their children would overlook the limits of parental control. As young people become more independent, they spend time in settings that adults cannot fully supervise and may deliberately reject reasonable guidance. Friends, online influences and individual decisions can all affect what happens. Parental conduct should therefore be assessed in relation to what parents knew and could realistically have done. Where neglect contributes to a problem, intervention may be justified, but automatic punishment risks treating responsible families as if they had authorised behaviour they tried to prevent.
blocks.guide: 区分影响力、控制能力与责任，适用于父母是否应受罚。

topics.description: 讨论家庭引导、早期干预与父母责任边界。

topics.title: S1 Ageing 人口老龄化
topics.name: 人口老龄化

blocks.title: S1A 服务需求与筹资压力
blocks.name: 服务需求与筹资压力
blocks.chain: more people require support relative to contributors → care demand rises → funding and staffing pressures
blocks.model: Population ageing can place pressure on public services when the number of people needing support grows faster than the resources available to provide it. More demand for care may require additional trained staff and facilities, while pension commitments must be financed over a longer period. The challenge becomes greater if the contributing workforce does not expand sufficiently. However, age alone does not determine dependency, and older people differ widely in health and circumstances. Policy should therefore examine actual care needs, productivity and funding arrangements rather than assuming that every increase in average age produces the same burden.
blocks.guide: 比较需求与供给的相对变化，避免老人数量直接等于负担。

blocks.title: S1B 老年人的持续贡献
blocks.name: 老年人的持续贡献
blocks.chain: experience and available time → mentoring care or volunteering → support for workplaces and communities
blocks.model: Older adults can continue to make important contributions through experience, care and community participation. Someone who has spent many years in a profession may help younger colleagues recognise difficulties that are not obvious from formal instruction alone. Others support families by providing care or take part in local organisations that depend on volunteers. These activities create value even when they are not all reflected in paid employment. Recognising such contributions gives a fuller account of population ageing and supports policies that allow people to remain involved in ways suited to their abilities and preferences.
blocks.guide: 区分有偿就业与其他贡献，用具体活动避免抽象夸奖。

blocks.title: S1C 灵活工作与照护调整
blocks.name: 灵活工作与照护调整
blocks.chain: work and services adapted to abilities → participation maintained → pressure partly reduced
blocks.model: Societies can respond to ageing by adapting work and support to people's changing needs. Flexible hours or less physically demanding roles may allow some older adults to remain employed when a conventional full-time position would be unsuitable. Community assistance can also help people manage everyday tasks without requiring more intensive care immediately. These arrangements may preserve participation and make better use of available resources. Their suitability must be assessed individually, since extending working lives is less realistic for people in poor health or occupations that place heavy physical demands on workers.
blocks.guide: 措施与能力差异匹配，避免统一延迟退休被写成万能方案。

topics.description: 比较老龄化的服务压力、经验贡献与灵活安排。

topics.title: S2 Family Structure 家庭结构
topics.name: 家庭结构

blocks.title: S2A 大家庭与资源共享
blocks.name: 大家庭与资源共享
blocks.chain: resources and responsibilities shared → practical and emotional support → greater resilience
blocks.model: Extended families can provide a useful support network by sharing responsibilities across several adults. When a parent faces a demanding work schedule, another family member may help with childcare or everyday tasks. Shared resources can also make unexpected difficulties easier to manage, since the burden does not fall entirely on one person. Regular contact may provide emotional reassurance as well. These advantages depend on cooperative relationships and an acceptable distribution of work; living together offers less support when responsibilities are imposed unfairly or family members have little privacy.
blocks.guide: 先写支持如何运作，再将关系质量设为条件。

blocks.title: S2B 小家庭与自主性
blocks.name: 小家庭与自主性
blocks.chain: fewer shared decisions → greater control over routines → privacy and mobility
blocks.model: Smaller households can give individuals greater control over how they organise daily life. People may find it easier to choose a work schedule, arrange their living space or move for a suitable opportunity when fewer household members are affected by the decision. Privacy can also allow adults to manage personal matters without continuous negotiation. These freedoms may be especially valuable to people whose plans differ from those of their wider families. The benefit should nevertheless be considered alongside the practical support they would need to arrange independently when illness or other difficulties arise.
blocks.guide: 自主性要对应具体决策，而不是只列 freedom 和 privacy。

blocks.title: S2C 独居与社会孤立
blocks.name: 独居与社会孤立
blocks.chain: limited accessible support → difficulties handled alone → vulnerability may increase
blocks.model: Living alone may increase vulnerability when a person also lacks reliable support outside the home. During illness or a period of emotional difficulty, there may be nobody nearby to notice a problem or provide immediate practical help. Repeatedly managing such situations without assistance can make everyday life more demanding. However, household size is an imperfect measure of social connection. Someone living alone may maintain strong friendships and community ties, while a person in a large household may feel unsupported. The relevant issue is the availability and quality of relationships that can be relied upon.
blocks.guide: 以支持是否可获得判断孤立，区分居住方式与关系质量。

topics.description: 权衡资源共享、个人自主与社会孤立。

topics.title: S3 Parenthood and Fertility 生育时间与生育率
topics.name: 生育时间与生育率

blocks.title: S3A 养育成本与生育推迟
blocks.name: 养育成本与生育推迟
blocks.chain: high costs and career penalties → parenthood feels difficult to sustain → delay or fewer planned children
blocks.model: People may postpone parenthood when the financial and professional costs appear difficult to manage. Housing, childcare and education expenses can create commitments that extend well beyond the immediate cost of having a child. If reducing working hours would also damage career prospects, prospective parents may feel that they must first establish greater security. Some will delay the decision, while others may decide to have fewer children than they originally intended. Policies aimed at supporting families therefore need to address the conditions that make parenting compatible with a stable livelihood.
blocks.guide: 区分推迟与减少生育，解释经济支出和机会成本如何共同作用。

blocks.title: S3B 持续低生育率与未来劳动力
blocks.name: 持续低生育率与未来劳动力
blocks.chain: smaller birth cohorts → fewer future labour-market entrants → adjustment in funding and production needed
